The base template: menus, death and fallbacks

New games are seeded with editable boilerplate before the first room. Use it as a recommended starting point when it fits, or extend or replace any part to serve the brief. These are ordinary game resources, with no protected ownership or reserved template ranges.

- Logic 0 builds the menu bar once on boot (File: Save, Restore, Restart, Quit; Speed; Sound; Help), binds the classic keys (ESC opens the menu, F5/F7/F9 save, restore and restart, F1 shows help, TAB lists the inventory), turns the status line on, then runs call.v(v0) so your room logic runs first every cycle. After the room returns, logic 0 answers the menu controllers and, once per submitted line, prints the parser fallback: "I don't know the word" when the line carried an unknown word, "I don't understand that" when no said() matched. A room that answers a line without a said() match should set(f4) after its own reply so the template does not add the generic one.
- Death is a shared handler: print your death line, then call(255). It stops input and movement, plays the death sound and offers the Restore, Restart or Quit box — SPACE steps the choice, ENTER confirms, 1-3 choose directly, F7/F9/Alt-Z answer directly. A cancelled or failed restore returns to the box; the player stays dead rather than walking in a broken control mode. If you replace this handler, design and playtest the recovery or continuation behavior your game needs.
- Read logic 0 and logic 255 for their current state, controller and string usage before editing; their sources are available through read_logic. Update affected references together when reusing IDs or changing conventions. Automatic allocation avoids IDs used by the current code; explicit bindings and edits can coordinate a rewrite. Playtest boot, input and any menu/death behavior affected by your changes. A fair death still needs a fair cause: the hazard belongs in your room's picture and priority plane.

rooms.title: The Castle Gate
rooms.description: Opening room. Wenna stands before Thornwall's gate. A royal notice on a post, bread on a bench (wrapped in a brass-polishing cloth: the first discovery) and a lit brass lantern on a hook. An alligator drifts in the moat; swimming earns a warning, then death. The drawbridge leads north into the hall; the path runs east to the meadow.

rooms.title: The Great Hall
rooms.description: King Brannoc sits beside the kingdom's last candle. Talk to him to accept the errand of the Three Bright Things (10). Return with Bell, Ember and Map to restore Thornwall and finish the story (60). He drops hints about each errand.

rooms.title: The Meadow Crossroads
rooms.description: A signpost where the road forks: west to the castle, north along the river to the gorge, east to the stove hut, south to the old oak. The first of three roadside candles stands here, unlit; light it with the lantern.

exits.name: South to the old oak and well

rooms.title: The River Gorge
rooms.description: A heron stands in the shallows and wants to discuss the bread. Give it the bread and it ferries Wenna across/down the river (20). The Bell lies underwater in the gorge pool; the heron's help lets Wenna recover it (40). A second roadside candle sits on a rock.

rooms.title: The Stove Hut
rooms.description: A hut with a crooked smoking chimney. A vain salamander lives in the stove and guards the undying Ember. It is easily impressed by polished brass: polish the lantern with the cloth and show it, and it trades the Ember, carried safely in the lantern (40).

rooms.title: The Old Oak and the Talking Well
rooms.description: An old woman knits with map-thread under the oak; the talking well beside her knows the answers to things. Solve her riddle (wrong answers earn hints, the well gives clues) to receive the wandering Map (40). The third roadside candle hangs in the oak.

messages: Thornwall's gate stands open across the drawbridge. The Great Hall lies beyond it, and the king is waiting. A royal notice is posted by the moat, bread sits on the bench and a lantern burns on its hook. The path east runs into the meadow.
Castle Thornwall stands across the moat, gray and patched. The drawbridge leads into the Great Hall. A notice is posted by the moat, and the path runs east into the meadow.
A lantern burns on a hook by the path.
The alligator says nothing. It gives the impression of listening, and of thinking about lunch.
Far beyond the hills, smoke rises from a crooked chimney. Someone out there keeps a fire going day and night.
